evidenceClass: Windows automated browser infrastructure and wire capability verification
provenance: Measured before commit from the dirty implementation at this parent revision. Source identities below describe final reviewed files; individual earlier runs retain their own harness hashes. These records are historical evidence, not contracts or a resumable prepared handoff.
limits: No hosted Linux execution: WSL is not installed and no hosted run was launched. CI includes the protocol check and existing cleanup/fault checks.
Installed and integration validation used SwiftShader; benchmark smokes report an Intel non-fallback adapter in headless Chrome. No manual visual/audible or visible physical-GPU performance claim.

Browser benchmark uses one-second warmup/two-second sampling; content uses its existing exploratory mode (20 samples per workload). Neither establishes a performance baseline or historical budget comparison.
The content input is the existing local archived migration fixture, not a newly selected real-consumer conformance proof.

Selected raw records only: full package/build/profile directories, screenshot pixels, benchmark snapshots/traces and browser logs remain local. Protocol snapshot/trace counts and hashes are retained; raw sampling is gzip retained separately.

A restricted protocol attempt failed Chrome/process inspection. The first headed benchmark reported a hidden page and timed out with successful cleanup. A subsequent headless attempt found an initialization-order bug, corrected before final acceptance. One initial full-suite run lost the installed test process without a diagnostic; focused and subsequent full suites passed.

validation.wireFragmentation: Deterministic TCP peer sent a fragmented 5 MiB reply with a split UTF-8 code point, split frame header and interleaved ping.
validation.partialStartup: Missing executable and live owned preview startup failures release resources; diagnostics and original failures remain distinct.
